themes_detail.label: Bus Stop Shelter Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Bus stop shelter complaints spiked to 4 this week compared to a 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 4.95)—suggesting rapid deterioration of transit infrastructure in East Harlem that may be leaving commuters without weather protection.
evidence: 4 bus stop shelter complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)
Statistically significant deviation indicating acute new problem rather than chronic issue
Aligns with longstanding CB budget request for transit/transportation improvements
reporting_angles: Field visit to identify which specific bus stops are non-functional and interview commuters about impact on daily transit experience
MTA statement on whether shelters are under repair or maintenance backlog; tie to broader East Harlem transit equity concerns

themes_detail.label: Elevator Outages in Buildings
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 5 last week versus a 0.8 weekly baseline—a 567% spike (z-score: 4.39)—pointing to a sudden wave of building code violations or maintenance failures affecting residents' access to apartments.
evidence: 5 elevator complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (567% increase, z-score: 4.39)
Concentrated spike suggests coordinated failure or enforcement action rather than random incidents
DOB data shows 569 total permit filings with 474 alterations—possible connection to renovation-related elevator issues
reporting_angles: Cross-reference DOB permits with elevator complaint locations; investigate whether renovations or deferred maintenance is causing outages
Interview residents in affected buildings about how disabled/elderly residents are managing without functioning elevators; landlord accountability

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park rules violations exploded to 4 complaints 2 weeks ago from a 0.2 weekly average—a 1,500% spike (z-score: 8.66, highest severity)—indicating either a specific enforcement campaign or deteriorating park conditions/user conduct requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 4 park rules violation complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,500% spike, highest z-score: 8.66)
Most statistically extreme spike in data, indicating either acute new problem or sudden policy shift
Aligns with CB budget request for park improvements and maintenance
reporting_angles: Identify which parks saw violations; determine if spike reflects new NYPD enforcement, specific incident, or actual increase in problematic behavior
Interview Parks Department and local precinct; talk to park users and community advocates about what triggered complaints

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Wave
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints nearly quadrupled to 9 last week from a 2.2 weekly average—a 300% increase (z-score: 3.94)—indicating a sudden sanitation crisis that may be linked to street condition complaints and community board's longstanding graffiti/cleanup requests.
evidence: 9 illegal dumping complaints last week vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% spike, z-score: 3.94)
Street condition complaints at 453 over 90 days suggest broader sanitation/maintenance infrastructure strain
CB has repeatedly requested graffiti removal/cleaning increases, indicating chronic underfunding of Sanitation
reporting_angles: Map illegal dumping complaint clusters; investigate whether specific blocks or neighborhoods lack Sanitation enforcement or commercial waste management
Interview Sanitation Commissioner about whether recent policy changes or staffing cuts are contributing; get community response on public health impact

themes_detail.label: Obstruction & Lost Property Spikes
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints (5, +300% vs 1.2 baseline) and lost property reports (6, +433% vs 1.1 baseline)—both emerging 2 weeks ago with z-scores above 5.0—suggest either increased foot traffic/crowding or a policing/reporting behavior shift worth understanding.
evidence: Obstruction complaints: 5 two weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (300% spike, z-score: 5.67)
Lost property complaints: 6 two weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (433% spike, z-score: 5.26)
Concurrent timing suggests shared root cause (e.g., event, transit disruption, or reporting campaign)
reporting_angles: Determine if spikes correlate with a specific event, construction project, or transit service change in East Harlem
Investigate whether NYPD increased civilian complaint reporting or whether actual obstructions/lost items increased
